The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 499df173e9f8ba2d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 8-9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: There are a dense smooth open Y ◦ ⊂ V , a po- larizable pure rational variation V on Y ◦ with an invariant lattice and quasi-unipotent boundary monodromy, and a nonzero algebraic map u : OY ◦ (−LY ) −→ Ed , Ep = Grp F (V ⊗ OY ◦ ), Fd+1 V = 0. (3.2) REVERSE LOGARITHMIC KODAIRA INEQUALITY 9 On every model (Y ′, D′) just described, the rationally identified map and all its Higgs iterates θj (u) : OY ′ (−LY ′ ) 99K Ed−j ⊗ (B′ )⊗j (3.3) have regular coefficients at every prime of Y ′ in the preceding sense. Here the variation and its Hodge bundles are understood over the common dense open, and a grade outside their range is zero. The same statement holds for the homogeneous tensor replacement used in Theorem 4.1. More precisely, if u∗ is obtained from u by homogeneous tensor operations of positive degree a and flat Hodge-compatible projections, then u∗ : O(−aLY ′ ) 99K E0, θj (u∗) : O(−aLY ′ ) 99K Ej ⊗ (B′ )⊗j (3.4) have the same coefficient property. Here A is the resulting pure variation, p∗ is its highest nonzero Hodge index, and Ej = Grp∗−j F A. Finite levels and a common further unipotent ramification may be used in these assertions.
